title: Priv IAM Operator Kit: Terraform module for least-privilege roles and bindings
creator: Maya Chen
description: Create a reusable Terraform module ("iam-operator-kit") that provisions minimal, auditable IAM roles and RBAC bindings for Private (VPC) deployments. The module should support: service-account role binding templates, automated ephemeral access patterns, granular resource-level policies, easy upgrade paths for existing stacks, and built-in runtime health checks. Aim to provide a best-practices starter kit for customers and internal installs that reduces privilege surface while keeping developer ergonomics.
acceptance_criteria: Module exposes a small set of inputs (project_id/vpc_id, tenancy_type, role_templates, sa_prefix) and outputs (role_ids, binding_ids, policy_documents) documented in README
Module creates least-privileged IAM roles for common Redwood components (control-plane, runtime-proxy, metrics-ingest) with parameterized scoping
Supports opt-in ephemeral roles via short-lived credentials (sts, workload identity) with example usage in examples/ephemeral/
Includes idempotent upgrade path: migration helper scripts and a dry-run plan step to surface binding changes before apply
Module has Terraform plan/apply unit tests in CI (terratest or kitchen-terraform) and passes security linting (tfsec, checkov) in pipeline
Health-check outputs (cloudwatch/exporter metrics) emitted as terraform outputs and sample dashboard panels provided
Security team sign-off obtained and security review checklist completed
Documentation and example deploys added to internal module catalog and Confluence guide
work_done: Gathered patterns from 5 customer private installs and internal Dedicated setups (notes in Confluence)
Wrote initial module skeleton (main.tf, variables.tf, outputs.tf, README.md) with provider-agnostic interfaces
Implemented role templates for control-plane, runtime, and metrics with least-privilege permission sets
Built examples/ephemeral demonstrating STS-based short-lived creds and workload-identity binding
Added basic tfsec and checkov configs and ran against module; iterated on policy scoping to remove wildcard permissions
Created initial Terratest suite validating role creation, binding idempotency, and sample policy simulation
Opened draft GitHub PR: github.com/redwood-inference/infra-modules/pull/842 (module skeleton + tests)
decisions_and_tradeoffs: Choosing provider-agnostic inputs increases surface area but eases future GCP/Azure support; decided to prioritize AWS for first release while keeping interfaces generic
Ephemeral access implemented via STS token exchange rather than building a custom broker to keep scope limited and defer long-lived secrets handling
We split role templates into small composable pieces rather than one monolithic policy to make least-privilege auditing easier
Migration strategy favors non-destructive binding adds with an explicit reconciliation job to remove deprecated bindings in a follow-up to reduce blast radius
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: accidental broad permissions in early templates — Mitigation: mandatory tfsec/checkov gates and security review before merge
Risk: upgrade could cause transient permission gaps — Mitigation: provide dry-run migration tool and staged rollout steps in playbook
Risk: customers with older private installs may have custom role names — Mitigation: add name-translation helpers and discovery scripts to module examples
